title: Truth
tomorrow: two friends, one fight, and Grace stuck in the middle. now what?

cards: Somebody steps away from a microphone, or out of an interview, or off a stage, and asks: be honest, was it bad? Every answer has two parts: the words, and the voice that carries them.
A sentence can be accurate and still land like a slap. Ephesians asks for both parts at once: “speaking the truth in love.” So what does that sound like, out loud?

teach.h: TRUTH IN LOVE, SO SOMEONE GROWS.
teach.b: The full line: “But speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things.” Truth without love can be cruel. Love without truth can be a pleasant lie that leaves someone unready.
The goal in that verse is growth: the truth is spoken so someone can grow.

teach.h: A SOFT ANSWER TURNETH AWAY WRATH.
teach.b: Proverbs listens to the sound of it: “A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.” Same facts, different voice, different result.
And: “A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.” Fitly means fitting: the right word at the right moment, set like gold in a silver frame.
John's Gospel says of Jesus that he was “full of grace and truth,” both at once, not taking turns. So much of the craft is in the voice. Say what worked first, because that's true too.
Then say the one thing that matters most, plainly, at a moment they can hear it. Then stay.
Truth spoken in love doesn't drop the hard part and walk off.

how: Christians practice honesty through confession, accountability friendships and community life; some churches teach Matthew 18's way of speaking to someone privately first when there is a wrong to name.

o: whatever feels right to the one speaking
a fact that matters only if it can be proved
what's real, said so the other person can grow

games.q: the sound of truth — tap the pairs.

s: speaking the truth in love means softening it until it isn't true
both halves at once: truth, and love; the goal is growth.
Proverbs says a soft answer turneth away wrath
and grievous words stir up anger.
John says Jesus was full of truth rather than grace
full of grace and truth: both, not taking turns.

games.q: a coworker asks you to read her cover letter tonight. it has the company's name spelled wrong. what fits apples of gold?
o: tell her now, kindly, with what's strong about the letter too.
say it looks great; she's nervous enough already.
mark every flaw in red so nothing gets missed.
games.why: a word fitly spoken: true, at the right time, and kind enough to be heard.

practice: Think of one true thing you've been holding back from someone, something they'd be better for hearing. Say it out loud, quietly, as you'd say it to them: once plainly, then once more in the softest voice that is still honest.
Listen to the difference in your own voice, and keep the second one.

wordCard.voice: Truth. Saying what's real, in a voice that wants the other person to grow.

orig.note: Greek: being truthful. the word behind 'speaking the truth' in Ephesians 4:15.

carryVoice: Your line: truth in love, both halves at once, the way grace and truth came together. See you tomorrow.
